beats.intro: Chapter fifty-nine. [[sub]]Adding radicals works just like combining like terms.
beats.parts: Every radical has two parts. [[idx]]The small number in the crook is the index: here, three, for a cube root. [[rad]]The number under the sign is the radicand: negative sixteen. [[two]]A square root has index two, even though we don't write it. [[coef]]A number in front, like the thirteen in thirteen times the cube root of two hundred, is the coefficient: it multiplies the radical.
beats.like: Radicals with the same index and the same radicand are like radicals. [[think]]Think of the square root of five as a single object, like x. [[seven]]Three root five plus four root five is three of them plus four of them: [[ans]]seven root five. [[keep]]Only the coefficients add. The index and the radicand stay the same, just as x stays x when you add three x and four x. [[sub]]Subtraction works the same way: nine root five minus six root five is three root five.
beats.unlike: Unlike radicals can't be combined. [[ex]]The square root of two plus the square root of three [[no]]is not the square root of five. [[chk]]Check with decimals: about one point four one plus one point seven three is about three point one four, while the square root of five is about two point two four. [[leave]]So the square root of two plus the square root of three stays as it is.
beats.simp: Sometimes radicals only look unlike. [[ex]]Take the square root of twelve plus eight root three. [[s1]]Simplify the square root of twelve first: it's two root three. [[now]]Now both terms are multiples of root three, [[ans]]so two root three plus eight root three is ten root three. [[rule]]Always simplify each radical before deciding what can be combined.
beats.mixed: Here's a longer one, with cube roots. [[ex]]The cube root of one hundred twenty-eight, minus the cube root of fifty-four, plus the cube root of twenty-four. [[s1]]Simplify each one: [[a]]four times the cube root of two, [[b]]three times the cube root of two, [[c]]and two times the cube root of three. [[comb]]The first two are like radicals: four minus three is one. [[ans]]The result is the cube root of two plus two times the cube root of three, and that's as far as it goes.
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[w1]]A radical has an index, a radicand, and possibly a coefficient. [[w2]]Like radicals share the same index and radicand: add or subtract their coefficients. [[w3]]Unlike radicals can't be combined. [[w4]]Simplify each radical first, because some will turn out to be alike. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.finish: Great work. That's the end of chapter fifty-nine, adding and subtracting radicals.
